To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The 5' end (approximately 100 nt) of nematode 18S rDNA barcoding region is highly variable at the family level, 2) Alignment scores and identity scores are highly variable within nematode families, and 3) Alignment score thresholds for nematode family level identification can be determined based on the alignment scores produced by BLAST for a representative set of sequences.

(a) alignment score is a more reliable indicator for taxonomic identification than the identity score and (b) taxon-specific thresholds for both similarity scores are required to achieve high taxonomic accuracy in metabarcoding of marine free-living nematodes.
the similarity scores of 5'end of 18S nematode barcode are highly variable, and this variability is not related to taxonomic distance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the variability of 18S barcoding region expressed by similarity scores in marine nematodes? What is the impact of the variability on taxonomy assignment? What are the similarity scores thresholds that can be used for reliable assignment of marine nematode 18S barcodes to family level taxon categories?
the evaluation of 5' region of 18S barcoding region of marine nematode species and the development of similarity thresholds for reliable identification of barcodes to family level taxon categories.
the evaluation of similarity scores produced by BLAST and their variability in the context of nematode taxonomy assignment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no single similarity score threshold that can be applied to all marine nematode taxa, and that the best similarity score threshold to use depends on the taxonomic level, the nematode taxonomic category, and the number of sequences in the reference database.
similarity scores are useful in taxonomy assignment of nematodes, but they should not be used as the sole criteria for identification of anonymous OTU to family level taxon.
there is no universal similarity threshold for nematode 18S rDNA barcode, and that the threshold value should be determined for each nematode taxon based on the variability of its 5' end barcode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(i) similarity score variability of nematodes is higher at lower levels of taxonomy; (ii) the variability of similarity scores increases with increasing genetic distance; (iii) nematodes belonging to the same family can have similarity scores that are higher or lower than the similarity threshold for the family; and (iv) similarity scores of nematodes belonging the same family can be higher than the threshold for the next higher taxonomic level.

the use of alignment score and identity score thresholds in the taxonomy assignment process should be avoided, since these similarity measures are highly variable and do not provide consistent and accurate taxonomic assignment.
the alignment scores are not reliable enough to be used as a similarity threshold for the assignment of marine nematode barcodes to family level taxon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single similarity threshold for the whole nematode family cannot be recommended.

the variability of the 5' end nematode 18S rDNA barcoding region can be expressed in terms of similarity scores and that these scores can be used to determine taxon specific similarity cutoffs that can be applied to identify barcodes to family taxonomic level.
the similarity scores produced by BLAST are variable and should not be used for taxon specific similarity threshold determination.
